title: How to compare MDR providers when every proposal looks promising
content_md: Choosing a managed detection and response (MDR) provider means committing budget, connecting systems, and trusting another team to act when your organization is under pressure. Yet a proposal promising 24x7 coverage, expert analysts, and fast response can leave important questions unanswered. Which systems will actually be monitored? What will analysts investigate before contacting you? What happens when an incident needs more work? Before choosing a provider or renewing your current agreement, ask for evidence of how the service operates. Rapid7’s MDR Evaluation Scorecard gives you 18 checks to structure that conversation and record what still needs proving. Start with one investigation Ask a provider to walk you through a completed investigation, using an anonymized example where necessary. Follow the initial signal through the evidence considered, the analyst’s decision, and any response actions. Suppose suspicious activity involves an account with access to a critical business system. Can the provider show how the account’s permissions, the systems within reach, and known weaknesses influenced its investigation? Can it explain what it ruled out and why it escalated or contained the activity? This exercise helps you assess whether exposure context, intelligence, and customer telemetry work together.
